correctness.rationale: Substitution from the primary model gives an exact scalar threshold 21/38 and a=b=1/2. The scalar threshold map preserves each threshold half-interval, giving y(t)=P^t[σ+a^t(y0−σ)] and all-state exponential convergence. Möbius inversion counts exact primitive necklaces. Each forced affine m-step map has norm at most a^m<1, and its unique periodic solution has error ≤aε/(1−a); the prethreshold perturbation is ≤ε/(1−a), strictly less than the binary threshold margins. This proves genuine, locally exponentially attracting prime cycles under the stated norm bound. The exact off-diagonal-positive example has ε≤1/10<17/76. The embedded checker replays exact rational finite tests; those tests are not asserted to prove the infinite-family theorem.

originality.rationale: Source-level comparison: the 2026 original supplies the best-response update but reports equilibrium results and a conjectural prospect of universal convergence; it does not supply rotation cycles, a necklace census, or robust arbitrary-period attractors. The prior 2023 and 2025 convergence theorems concern different coordination payoffs and restricted activation/network assumptions, so their hypotheses do not cover this public-goods synchronous construction. Six actual semantic database queries and accessible historical claim searches yielded no statement implying this claim. Originality of the exact model-specific construction is supported, though a broader threshold-map theorem could encompass it.

value.rationale: The original 2026 research explicitly proposes a universal equilibrium-convergence result. An all-dimension, globally classified family of counterexamples within its permitted synchronous update class shows why that conjecture needs a restricted revision or topology hypothesis. The persistence theorem removes fragility of pure permutation influence, exhibiting the phenomenon for positive weight on every directed interaction. The necklace enumeration and exact parameter/norm bounds allow reproducible structural benchmarks rather than only a small simulated cycle.
